tagline: Bayou towns with rivers doing the heavy work.
intro: From Simmesport, the northernmost town on the Atchafalaya, the drive reaches Morganza near the Mississippi, then turns through the bayou towns toward Plaquemine. There, Bayou Plaquemine once gave southwestern Louisiana a water route to the great river.

Morganza sits at the lower end of a sharp bend in the Mississippi, and levees broke there or just downriver in 1850, 1865, 1867 and 1890. Just north of town, the Morganza Spillway, built from 1939 to 1955, can turn the river's high water down into the Atchafalaya Basin.

moments.title: Simmesport
moments.text: The town stands on the west bank of the Atchafalaya near Old River, which connects the Red and Atchafalaya rivers with the Mississippi.

moments.title: Maringouin
moments.text: Highway 77 passes through a town named for the mosquito, with Bayou Grosse Tete along its eastern border.

moments.title: Plaquemine Lock State Historic Site
moments.text: George Goethals, later the Panama Canal's chief engineer, designed this lock; it opened in 1909, closed in 1961 when river traffic outgrew it, and its lockhouse is now the museum.
